headline: Medibank CEO highlights premium cost pressure, payout ratio and value initiatives as key consumer metrics
reasoning: David Koczkar notes Medibank's claims payout ratio is higher than the industry average, framing this as evidence consumers are getting value. The company has invested $300 million in additional customer value and health and wellbeing initiatives. Koczkar flags rising aggregator costs — nearly doubling in two years — as a systemic cost pressure on premiums, arguing that only one quarter of aggregator-driven sales attracted new customers to the market, suggesting commission-driven churn. He has raised the issue with government and at the CEO forum, advocating for greater transparency and scrutiny of all costs in the private health sector to keep premium pressure down.
quote: Well, I think we will focus enormous energy in keeping pressure off premiums, which is why, um, we see our payout ratio, our claims payout ratio as being higher than the industry average. Really, the test for consumers about whether they're getting a good deal. Uh, equally, we've invested in providing more value to the customers $300 million of value and also supporting more customers in the health and well-being, which is actually what our consumers want. I would say, though, that we are seeing the rise of aggregators in the market. The cost of aggregators, uh, in the industry has almost doubled in two years, and I think consumers deserve options to and we would promote choice and comparison. But unfortunately, the only true source of comparison is the government's website. Aggregators do not feature all funds or all products. And so, you know, this cost has been growing in plain sight. And if we're serious about keeping pressure off premiums, we need every cost in the private health sector, whether it be hospitals, insurers, medical professionals or now aggregators to be treated with the same scrutiny.
episode_title: Medibank's growth prescription for a healthy profit

headline: Medibank CEO advocates shift from treatment to prevention and expansion of community care as strategic priorities for the Australian health system.
reasoning: Koczkar outlined Medibank's strategic focus on investing in prevention rather than treatment, the rise of community care as a care setting, digitising health, and personalising health services. He framed these as advocacy positions with government and as areas of active investment for the company, including through the Medibank Health division which grew profits more than 31% in the year.
quote: We're particularly focused on, uh, moving from what is effectively a treatment system to one that invest more in prevention. We're actively investing in the rise of community care is being part of the care setting. We're looking at digitizing health and also making health more personal. And there are the things that we are advocating for.
episode_title: Medibank's growth prescription for a healthy profit
